title: Crestline Credit Card Promotional Plans: One Plan per Ticket and Savings Order
content:
A Crestline Credit Card ticket carries at most one promotional plan (1 per ticket). A deferred-interest plan and an equal-payment plan are therefore mutually exclusive on the same ticket, and the cardholder chooses one among those the purchase qualifies for.

## Savings and the promotional minimum

Crestline instant savings and set savings are taken off the ticket before it posts, so the promotional minimum is compared with the **posted amount after those savings**. The two benefits stack in that order and never the other way round.

Hypothetical ticket: a tire set priced at 1,060 USD with 80 USD of instant savings posts at 980 USD. Against a plan minimum of 999 USD, the posted 980 USD does not qualify, although the price before savings was above it.

## Tickets are taken as they are

- Two tickets cannot be combined to reach a promotional minimum.
- One ticket cannot be split to place part on a plan and part as a standard purchase.

## Fleet and personal charges stay apart

A ticket charged to a Crestline fleet account never posts to a personal Crestline Credit Card, and a personal card ticket is never re-billed to a fleet account.

## Points of judgement

| Situation | Outcome |
|---|---|
| A ticket qualifies for both a 12-month deferred plan and a 24-month equal-payment plan | the cardholder chooses one; the ticket carries only that plan |
| Two tickets of 300 USD each against a 499 USD minimum | each is compared alone; neither reaches it |
| A ticket of 1,200 USD where the cardholder wants 999 USD on a plan and the rest standard | not possible; the ticket is taken whole |
